what: Spare Key's reader and rules (tools/real-inpage.mjs) run inside each real settings page of the builder's own Google, Gmail and Amazon account, in the builder's own Chrome, read-only and code only (no Gemini Nano). Only these codes and counts left each page. 'siteShows' was counted in the same page from its own links and labels (for example Google's 'Access to (3)'), also as numbers only.
method: Chrome automation pasted the bundle into each page and called __sk(checkId) or __skFrame(url, checkId). This is not the extension's own scan (runScan): the permission prompt, the scan tab and the 'Verify it's you' wait in the panel were not part of it. Google asked 'Verify it's you' on the devices, recovery and 2-Step pages; the builder confirmed with a passkey in the same tab.
